analysis: The only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md is a date bump (line 3) and one new table row at head line 572 that documents a `--prompt-prep` benchmark mode. Both are documentation edits with no code, config or protocol change in the supplied evidence. The row describes a CPU-only benchmark that loads only the tokenizer, so it does not touch model weights, the encrypted prefix cache, or attestation and authorization. No ProviderBenchmark code is supplied, so I could not verify that the mode behaves as described. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of a problem. The benchmark compares token IDs and decoded fields with the prompt token cache's background comparisons off. Real prompt content could appear in its JSON output, which would touch A-001 (consumer prompts). The row says the benchmark uses synthetic chat, agent and tool-loop conversations, and a local benchmark does not receive consumer traffic, so I see no exposure. The next pass should check that PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift uses only synthetic prompts and writes no files or logs with sensitive data. The rest of the file is unchanged. I did not re-evaluate pre-existing statements on logout, switch, cache or GLM qualification, nor T-041, which are outside the diff. No threat-model assumption is invalidated and no threat-model update is needed.
